source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Remove the Battery for 5 minutes.
2.Insert the battery again, boot into BIOS, check date/time would be reset.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this Clear CMOS case requires physically removing the CMOS battery from the motherboard for 5 minutes, then re-inserting it and booting to BIOS to confirm date/time reset. Removing/re-inserting the onboard battery is physical work only a person at the machine can do; agent cannot open the chassis or touch the battery.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator removes the CMOS battery for 5 min, re-inserts it, and boots to BIOS to confirm date/time were reset; agent cannot perform the physical battery removal.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: physical/hardware operation at the machine - human only; agent must not attempt.

original_test_intent: Verify five minutes without the CMOS battery resets BIOS date/time and that the SUT can return through BIOS to an approved operating configuration.
original_method: After configuration capture and complete approved power discharge, a qualified operator removes the correct motherboard battery for five minutes, reinstalls it with correct polarity, enters BIOS, observes date/time and other reset effects, and restores only approved settings.
manual_activity: Opening the chassis, removing/reinstalling the battery and observing BIOS are the core test and require a qualified operator; the agent cannot touch the board or claim the BIOS observation.
required_inputs: Exact battery location/type, polarity and holder procedure
Fully de-energized/discharged state and ESD controls
BIOS settings, boot/security-key and time baseline/backup
Expected reset scope, five-minute timing rule and restoration plan
Console/OOB recovery, operator and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Never handle the battery or motherboard while energized; confirm discharge and use ESD controls.
Stop on unknown battery, damaged holder, polarity uncertainty or unsafe chassis access.
Back up boot/security and configuration data because reset may affect more than date/time.
Preserve the first reset/boot outcome; do not automatically repeat battery removal.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only pre/post BIOS-exposed configuration, BMC/SEL, boot and OS health where interfaces allow.
Track the five-minute operator timestamps and compare approved configuration/time baselines.
Organize recovery evidence without performing hardware work or issuing the verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the battery/power/ESD and backup procedure.
Remove/reinstall the battery and inspect BIOS physically.
Restore approved settings, verify recovery and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No software command can replace the specified battery removal; its physical limitation is correct.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the exact physical method and use read-only firmware/boot telemetry only as corroboration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Battery removal, five-minute dwell, reinsertion, BIOS date/time check and the 5/20-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RETAIN BATTERY METHOD WITH CONFIGURATION RECOVERY CONTROL
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a board-specific de-energization checklist, timed battery custody record, before/after BIOS setting matrix and verified boot recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact motherboard and CMOS battery implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board revision, BIOS and BMC firmware.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner board service manual and BIOS reset/recovery specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe handling and wider reset/recovery traceability without replacing battery removal.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; date/time reset remains the named acceptance observation.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Board SOP, baseline/backup, reset scope and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A date/time change alone may not prove or bound all CMOS configuration effects.

project_override_considerations: A project may define additional settings that must be checked/restored, but a software defaults command cannot replace physical battery-removal coverage unless the test plan explicitly changes.
expected_evidence: Approved board/battery/power/ESD SOP, BIOS backup and reset expectations
Before/after BIOS date/time and relevant setting captures
Restored boot/security configuration, OS/BMC health and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Criteria repeat the procedure but still express the intended date/time reset; missing wider reset and recovery details are readiness gaps, not contradictory facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The required board-specific inputs can be supplied and a qualified operator can perform the defined physical method; this is MANUAL ONLY rather than inherently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree with NO and add configuration/boot safety and recovery evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with MANUAL ONLY and its wider CMOS reset assessment.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Keeps manual execution distinct from agent evidence collection and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Expands a date/time-only note into safe, reversible proof of the exact five-minute battery method and its broader BIOS consequences.
independent_technical_reasoning: The function under test is loss of CMOS retention after physical battery removal. Remote reset commands are not equivalent, and the BIOS observation plus board handling requires an operator, while telemetry can only support the record.
